content:
I noticed that isAutoDecl decl returns true if decl is a private name, which is quite common in the module system. This leaves a lot of linting of user-written code on the table.

Some linters are concerned with things like source readability and well-formedness of user-written declarations, and so should apply to private declarations, whereas some linters are indeed only concerned with the public interface.

My feeling is that isAutoDecl should be true to its name, while a new isPrivateOrAutoDecl should be used to exempt private declarations in linters that only care about the public interface.

I've made batteries#1831 to start on this. It violates some linters, but all things considered...not too many? A lot of unusedArguments, mostly. (56 violations in total.)

Does this seem reasonable?

I think this split is good! (And of course, we should audit the existing linters... so perhaps, this can be staged as

  • add isPrivateOrAutoDecl (copying the current code),
  • make all linters use that if they should,
  • fix violations of the other linters that should use isAutoDecl instead,
  • change the definitino of isAutoDecl

(with the second and third stage being parallelisable).
batteries#1835 does 1 and 2 for the Batteries linters; as far as I can tell only the docstring linters are specifically "public interface" linters. :)

Also, the environment linter framework that we have been upstreaming/building in the core, currently obeys the module system, so we do a public import, rather than a private one (which is the case for the current batteries runner) making private declarations not seen.
Shouldn't linting private declarations be only possible from Lean.Linterlinters?

That makes sense! I imagine that when declaration linting at the syntax level/in Lean.Linters becomes easier/widespread, many of these env_linters will become Lean.Linters, and they will still want to test if the declarations they’re linting are autogenerated via isAutoDecl. So I’m hoping this is general-purpose regardless of which linters actually use it :)
(But (tangent) speaking of using isAutoDecl in Lean.Linters, we should probably make it monad generic to avoid liftCoreM in anticipation of this :eyes:)

I've made batteries#1838, which adds a pure Environment.isAutoDecl and makes isAutoDecl a monad-generic wrapper for that in any monad with MonadEnv. (The pure version has some conceivable use cases, and we don't need to modify the environment as MonadEnv grants us, so I thought it made sense.)
Do you think it would be worth upstreaming it so that the core linting library uses the same thing?
Can core mark automatic declarations so that the detection can be more reliable? (it's currently name based)
